How to Validate and Present Your UGC-Entitled Degree on LinkedIn & Resume

With the rapid adoption of online education across India, more students and working professionals are pursuing online degree courses from UGC-approved universities. Many graduates often wonder how to correctly showcase their UGC entitled online degree on platforms like LinkedIn or in a professional resume.

Whether you have completed an online bachelor degree or a specialized online degree program, proper validation and presentation matter in today’s competitive job market. Employers are highly recognizing credible online degrees, especially when they are listed clearly with academic details and accreditation.
In this read, we will guide you on how to format, verify, and highlight your online education credentials, so your profile stands out with both confidence and credibility.
Why Proper Presentation Matters

The stigma around online degrees is fading, but only if they are presented professionally and backed by accredited institutions. Recruiters today are more concerned with what you have learned and how you apply it, not whether your degree came from a physical classroom or a virtual one.
However, misrepresenting your online degree program, omitting UGC details, or listing vague course names can harm rather than help your profile.
What Is a UGC Entitled Online Degree?

A UGC entitled online degree is an online qualification offered by a university recognized by the University Grants Commission (UGC) of India, under strict guidelines. These degrees carry equal value to on-campus degrees, provided the university is authorized to offer them. Before listing your degree, always verify:

items: The university’s name on the UGC-DEB portal
The official degree name and duration
Mode of delivery (online/distance)
Accreditation details

Step-by-Step Guide to Presenting Your Online Degree on LinkedIn
1. Add it to Your Education Section
Go to your LinkedIn profile → Click on “Add Education” → Fill in the fields as follows:

items: School: Dayananda Sagar University (or your institution’s name)
Degree: Bachelor of Business Administration (Online) / BCA (Online)
Field of Study: As per your program
Start – End Dates: Mention clearly
Description (Optional but Recommended): Mention that it’s a UGC entitled online degree program with virtual labs, live mentorship, and industry-aligned curriculum.

blocks.x: 2. Highlight the Online Mode Strategically
Don’t hide the fact that it’s an online degree instead, showcase the flexibility, tech tools, and self paced learning it provided. For example:
“Completed a fully online, UGC-approved BCA degree with hands-on virtual lab experience, real-time mentor support, and Python, Java, and SQL-based projects.”
3. Add Related Certifications or Skills
If your online degree course included certifications (e.g., Google Ads, Data Analytics, etc.), list them under the “Licenses & Certifications” section to strengthen your academic background.
4. Post About Your Journey

Sharing a post about your experience in an online degree program is a great way to connect with peers, recruiters, and educators. Talk about what you learned, how you balanced work and study, and any live project you undertook.
How to List Your Online Degree on Your Resume
✔ Include It in the Education Section
Use a format like this:
Bachelor of Business Administration (Online) Dayananda Sagar University (UGC Entitled) Completed: August 2025 | Mode: Fully Online
This clearly communicates:

items: The degree type
The university
Its UGC entitlement
The mode of learning

blocks.x: ✔ Emphasize Skills & Projects
Recruiters often scan for skills and application over the degree title. Ensure your resume highlights:

items: Projects completed during the course (with brief descriptions)
Industry tools mastered (e.g., Python, Tableau, Linux)
Soft skills gained from online learning (e.g., time management, independent problem-solving)

blocks.x: ✔ Use a Cover Letter to Expand

In your cover letter, you can explain why you chose the online education route perhaps for flexibility, upskilling while working, or geographic constraints and how it shaped your learning style and work ethic.
Why Employers Value UGC-Entitled Online Degrees
A UGC entitled online degree assures the employer of:

items: Recognized curriculum and assessments
Quality infrastructure (virtual labs, mentorship, LMS)
Continuous learning aligned with NEP 2020
Accountability and periodic reviews by governing bodies

blocks.x: Moreover, companies increasingly value digital-first learners, those who are comfortable with remote work tools, proactive communication, and flexible collaboration. Completing an online degree showcases all of this.
Common Mistakes to Avoid

items: Hiding the “online” aspect Today’s employers don’t mind the online tag. Just be transparent and confident about it.
Not verifying UGC status Only UGC-entitled programs have academic parity with regular degrees.
Leaving the “Education” section blank on LinkedIn You are missing a huge opportunity to improve your discoverability and trust factor.
Vague course titles Instead of “Online Program in Business,” write “Bachelor of Business Administration (Online), DSU – UGC Entitled”

blocks.x: FAQs
01. Can I mention an online degree on LinkedIn?
Yes, and you should. Just make sure to mention the institution, UGC status, and that it’s an online mode of learning.
02. Is a UGC entitled online degree valid for government jobs?
Yes. As per UGC guidelines, online degrees from entitled universities are recognized for employment and higher studies.
03. Should I add “Online” next to the degree name on my resume?
Yes, especially if it helps distinguish your learning model and shows your ability to adapt to digital learning environments.
04. How do I verify my degree’s UGC status?
You can verify the university’s entitlement to offer online degrees on the UGC-DEB official website.
05. Does DSU offer UGC entitled online degree programs?
